chapter: Other Philadelphia work and the union
title: Two weeks in a big band at the Club Cadix, Philadelphia
summary: Waters remembers a big band with Louie Metcalf at the Club Cadix on Chestnut Street that closed after two weeks when someone was killed outside; it led to the Charlie Johnson job.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: for Boston - you see, when I left Boston, I stayed in Boston 4 or 5 years, maybe a little bit longer, see. Then I came from Boston to Philadelphia. Well, this - now here's, there's something else I remember in Philadelphia. See, now this is something else I remember in Philadelphia. I tell you who was in the band, but I still can't remember the name of the band or the leader. But I tell you who was in the band - Metcalf -

Yeah, was in the band. We worked in the - and I remember the place where we worked. We worked a place called the Club Cadix, I think Chestnut Street. Anyway it's a high-class club, but it turned out to be low-class because somebody got killed in front of the door there, and it closed after 2 weeks. Now that was a big band. So I mean that was a big band, so I, that's why I - so I made a mistake when I said the first big band was Charlie Miller - Charlie Johnson. It wasn't, it was this band, that the first big band, for these two weeks. That's where I was recommended from the violin player who was in charge, musical director of this band, went down Atlantic City and saw Charlie Johnson's band. And he recommended me, and the place closed. See how it comes back to you, I mean, you know? See, it all come back -
What was the name of this band in -
I don't know the name of the band, all I know -
Louie Metcalf wasn't the leader, he was just a sideman -
No, no, he was just in, I remember Louie because, you know -
Yeah, yeah, that's it. And the other members I don't - is Louie still living?
Oh, Jesus. 'Cause he could tell you about it, you know.
I talked with him many, many times, fortunately.

Well, he could tell you about this band down in Philadelphia, it only lasted two weeks. It's only two weeks, that's all, and then it closed. Then I went with Charlie Bes-, Charlie Miller, then I s-, I mean with Charlie Johnson and I stayed with that band 10 years [ ].
